newsletter.markdown:
1. **Discovery & Translational Science**

- **Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** [STAT+]: Recognized for their pioneering discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.
- **Anthropic AI biolab discovers novel CRISPR-like enzyme system** [@BioStocks]: Multi-agent system utilizing roughly 950 simultaneous Claude instances identified novel genetic sequences in 21.5 hours.
- **Targeting CD4⁺ effector memory T cells re-expressing CD45RA suppressor galectin-7** [PubMed]: Identified as a multi-omics-guided therapeutic strategy for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
- **Senescence-independent SASP drives tumor-macrophage inflammatory cascade and therapeutic resistance** [PubMed]: Mechanistic finding in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).
- **Computational discovery of bacterial biofilm inhibitors** [PubMed]: Computational approach applied to identify inhibitors against catheter-associated urinary tract infections targeting HCV NS3/4A protease and SLC6 transporter ligands.

2. **Early Trials — Phase I–II**

- **[Biotech]** **Prilenia Therapeutics doses first patient in global Phase 1/2 trial of PM577a** [@BioStocks]: Evaluating the agent for H1069Q-mutated Wilson disease.
- **Subcutaneous atezolizumab feasibility study** [PubMed]: Prospective, single-arm Phase 2 evaluation of at-home administration in non-small cell lung cancer.

3. **Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III**

- **[Biotech]** **Vaxcyte reports positive topline Phase 3 data for VAX-31** [STAT+, BioPharmDiving, @BioStocks]: The 31-valent pneumococcal vaccine met all prespecified primary endpoints in the pivotal OPUS-1 adult trial, demonstrating comparable effectiveness to Prevnar 20 and Capvaxive across strains, with superiority on three unique strains. OPUS-2 and OPUS-3 data are expected in the first half of 2027.
- **[Big Pharma]** **AstraZeneca reports positive COPD trial results for tozorakimab** [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery]: The IL-33-targeted antibody reduced disease flare-ups in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
- **[Big Pharma]** **Eli Lilly evaluates oral GLP-1RA safiglipron in Phase 3** [Nature Medicine]: Once-daily oral safiglipron demonstrated non-inferiority to dapagliflozin for HbA1c reduction across all tested doses and superiority at 90 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes.
- **[Biotech]** **Vincerx Pharma completes enrollment in Phase 3 CATT1 study of cadisegliatin** [@BioStocks]: Evaluating the asset in type 1 diabetes, with topline data expected in mid-2027.
- **[Biotech]** **Coya Therapeutics completes full enrollment in Phase 2/3 ALSTARS trial of COYA 302** [@BioStocks]: Investigating the therapy for ALS, with topline data anticipated in early Q2 2027.
- **[Biotech]** **Revolution Medicines begins treating patients in Phase 3 RASolute 309 trial** [@BioStocks]: Evaluating rasonque (daraxonrasib) plus zoldonrasib as first-line treatment for metastatic RAS G12D pancreatic cancer.

4. **Regulatory & Approvals**

- **[Big Pharma]** **Eli Lilly secures FDA approval for Jaypirca in first-line CLL** [STAT+]: Expanded indication covers previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia and small lymphocytic lymphoma.
- **FDA issues Request for Information on ibogaine clinical research** [FDA]: Seeking public input, safety data, and protocol elements for early-phase clinical trial designs under the executive order on serious mental illness.
- **FDA updates oncology accelerated approval withdrawal tracking** [FDA]: Recent actions include the withdrawal of Zepzelca (lurbinectedin) in SCLC and Krazati (adagrasib) with cetuximab in colorectal cancer, alongside the addition of post-marketing verification requirements for recent approvals like Hyrnuo and Etcamah.

5. **Business & Strategy**

- **[Big Pharma]** **AstraZeneca opens new Kendall Square R&D center** [@BioStocks]: Facility established in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
- **[Biotech]** **Vaxcyte plans BLA submission for VAX-31 in first half of 2028** [@BioStocks]: Regulatory filing timeline contingent on upcoming 2027 Phase 3 readouts.

6. **Public Health & Policy**

- **CMS announces $90 payments for Medicare Part B premiums** [STAT+]: Pre-midterm policy initiative announced by President Trump aimed at seniors.
- **FDA advisory committees and public transparency framework reviewed** [FDA]: Agency highlights the utilization of roughly 50 technical and scientific advisory panels for independent regulatory guidance.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Oats, Heart Disease, and the Molecules within Oats](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EG5uNB-1n3Y) -- Physionic
        - The video examines the effects of oats on heart disease and blood lipids, citing randomized controlled trials involving hypercholesterolemic adults.
        - References include studies investigating oat consumption compared to alternative dietary items like noodles or rice on lipid profiles.
        - Specific research highlights include investigations into cholesterol-lowering effects induced by microbially produced phenolic metabolites and prebiotic impacts on gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids.
        - Epidemiological studies are cited regarding whole grain intake and the associated risks of coronary heart disease and myocardial infarction.
    - [410 ‒ The biology of pregnancy: physiologic adaptation, childbirth, and long-term maternal health](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIFD0Y6UVE0) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Peter Attia and maternal-fetal medicine specialist Dr. Kathryn Gray discuss pregnancy as a profound cardiovascular and metabolic stress test.
        - The episode covers early hormonal changes, prenatal nutrition, neural tube defects, and the physiology, diagnosis, and treatment of gestational diabetes.
        - Pathologies such as preeclampsia and HELLP syndrome are explored, detailing acute risks, genetic insights, and the use of antihypertensive medications.
        - Additional topics include long-term cardiometabolic health outcomes, labor mechanics, cesarean and vaginal delivery, breastfeeding, prenatal genetic screening via cell-free DNA, and maternal health research in the US.
    - [Why Oura May Be Better Off Staying Private](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/c_Kb1AXTHeQ) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Patrick E. Donohue analyzes Oura's hardware-software business model and evaluates the challenges the company would face if it decided to go public.
        - The discussion highlights why Oura might benefit from remaining a private entity while pursuing major corporate partnerships or acquisitions to sustain its long-term growth.
